title: 2 Samuel Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 21.

questions.question: What was the reason given by the LORD for the three years of famine during David's days?
options: Because David sinned against the LORD
Because Saul and his bloody house slew the Gibeonites
Because the Israelites broke the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Because Saul and his bloody house slew the Gibeonites
questions.explanation: The famine was because Saul and his bloody house slew the Gibeonites, as the LORD told David (2 Samuel 21:1).

questions.question: Who were the Gibeonites according to 2 Samuel 21?
questions.correctAnswer: Remnant of the Amorites
questions.explanation: The Gibeonites were not children of Israel but were remnant of the Amorites (2 Samuel 21:2).

questions.question: True or False: David enquired of the LORD about the famine.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David enquired of the LORD concerning the famine (2 Samuel 21:1).

questions.question: What did David ask the Gibeonites in order to make atonement?
options: What gold or silver they wanted
What he should do to make atonement so they would bless the LORD's inheritance
questions.correctAnswer: What he should do to make atonement so they would bless the LORD's inheritance
questions.explanation: David asked the Gibeonites what he should do to make atonement so they might bless the LORD's inheritance (2 Samuel 21:3).

questions.question: What did the Gibeonites refuse to accept from Saul's house?
questions.correctAnswer: Silver and gold
questions.explanation: The Gibeonites said they would not accept silver or gold of Saul or his house (2 Samuel 21:4).

questions.question: True or False: The Gibeonites wanted David to kill any man in Israel as atonement.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The Gibeonites explicitly said that David should not kill any man in Israel (2 Samuel 21:4).

questions.question: What did the Gibeonites request to be delivered to them for hanging?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven men from Saul's sons
questions.explanation: The Gibeonites asked for seven men of Saul's sons to be delivered to them to hang (2 Samuel 21:6).

questions.question: Who did King David spare from being handed over to the Gibeonites?
questions.correctAnswer: Mephibosheth, son of Jonathan
questions.explanation: David spared Mephibosheth, son of Jonathan, because of the LORD's oath between David and Jonathan (2 Samuel 21:7).

questions.question: True or False: The king handed over the two sons of Rizpah and the five sons of Michal to the Gibeonites.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David gave the two sons of Rizpah and the five sons of Michal into the hands of the Gibeonites (2 Samuel 21:8).

questions.question: Where did the Gibeonites hang the seven men from Saul's house?
questions.correctAnswer: In Gibeah of Saul
questions.explanation: The seven men were hanged in Gibeah of Saul (2 Samuel 21:6-9).

questions.question: What did Rizpah do after her sons were hanged?
options: She mourned in sackcloth and protected their bodies from birds and beasts
questions.correctAnswer: She mourned in sackcloth and protected their bodies from birds and beasts
questions.explanation: Rizpah spread sackcloth on a rock and guarded the bodies from birds and beasts (2 Samuel 21:10).

questions.question: Who informed David about Rizpah's actions?
questions.correctAnswer: It was told to David
questions.explanation: It was told to David what Rizpah had done (2 Samuel 21:11).

questions.question: What did David do after learning about Rizpah's vigil?
options: He took the bones of Saul and Jonathan from Jabeshgilead
He ordered more men to be handed over
questions.correctAnswer: He took the bones of Saul and Jonathan from Jabeshgilead
questions.explanation: David took the bones of Saul and Jonathan from Jabeshgilead after hearing about Rizpah (2 Samuel 21:12).

questions.question: In what order did these events occur in 2 Samuel 21: David enquires of the LORD, Gibeonites request seven men, Rizpah guards the bodies, or David retrieves Saul's bones?
options: David enquires of the LORD, Gibeonites request seven men, Rizpah guards the bodies, David retrieves Saul's bones
Gibeonites request seven men, David retrieves Saul's bones, Rizpah guards the bodies, David enquires of the LORD
David retrieves Saul's bones, Rizpah guards the bodies, David enquires of the LORD, Gibeonites request seven men
Rizpah guards the bodies, David enquires of the LORD, Gibeonites request seven men, David retrieves Saul's bones
questions.correctAnswer: David enquires of the LORD, Gibeonites request seven men, Rizpah guards the bodies, David retrieves Saul's bones
questions.explanation: The sequence is David enquires of the LORD (verse 1), Gibeonites request seven men (verses 5-6), Rizpah guards the bodies (verse 10), then David retrieves Saul's bones (verse 12).

questions.question: True or False: Saul sought to destroy the Gibeonites because of his zeal for Israel and Judah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Saul sought to slay the Gibeonites in his zeal for Israel and Judah (2 Samuel 21:2).

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What action did Rizpah take after the seven sons of Saul were hanged, and what does this show about her character?
options: She spread sackcloth on a rock and guarded the bodies to protect them from birds and beasts
She buried the bodies immediately to give them a proper burial
She mourned in the city but did not approach the bodies
She asked David to avenge their deaths
questions.correctAnswer: She spread sackcloth on a rock and guarded the bodies to protect them from birds and beasts
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 21:10 describes Rizpah spreading sackcloth on the rock and keeping watch over the bodies, preventing birds and beasts from touching them, showing her deep loyalty and mourning. This underscores the biblical virtue of faithfulness and devotion.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 21:12, where did David retrieve the bones of Saul and Jonathan from, and what significance does this have?
options: From the men of Jabeshgilead who had rescued them from Philistine hands
From the Philistine streets of Bethshan where they were hung
From the battlefield of Gilboa where they had fallen
From the city of Gibeah where Saul reigned
questions.correctAnswer: From the men of Jabeshgilead who had rescued them from Philistine hands
questions.explanation: David took the bones from the men of Jabeshgilead, who had earlier taken them from the Philistines (2 Samuel 21:12). This act demonstrates obedience to honoring the dead, a biblical principle of respect and integrity (verses 12-14).

questions.question: What was the result after David buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan as commanded?
options: God was intreated for the land, ending the famine
The Philistines launched another attack immediately
David was rejected by his people
questions.correctAnswer: God was intreated for the land, ending the famine
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 21:14 states that after the burial, God was intreated for the land, meaning He showed mercy and the famine ceased. This teaches about the power of repentance and obedience in restoring God's blessing.

questions.question: What challenge did David face during the battle with the Philistines as described in 2 Samuel 21:15-16?
options: David grew faint while fighting against a giant armed with a heavy spear
David was captured by the Philistines during the battle
David was wounded but defeated the Philistines alone
questions.correctAnswer: David grew faint while fighting against a giant armed with a heavy spear
questions.explanation: Verses 15-16 explain that David grew faint during the battle while facing Ishbibenob, a giant with a spear weighing 300 shekels of brass, illustrating the human vulnerability even of a great leader and the need for reliance on God's strength.

questions.question: How did Abishai respond when Ishbibenob attempted to kill David, and what does this teach about Christian community?
options: He rescued David by killing Ishbibenob, showing the importance of protecting one another
He prayed for David's safety but did not engage in battle
He fled the battle to save his own life
He encouraged David to fight alone to prove his strength
questions.correctAnswer: He rescued David by killing Ishbibenob, showing the importance of protecting one another
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 21:17 tells that Abishai saved David by killing the Philistine, demonstrating the biblical virtue of mutual support and the value of protecting fellow believers in times of danger.

questions.question: What instruction did David's men give him after Abishai saved his life, and why?
options: They told David not to go out to battle anymore to preserve the 'light of Israel'
They asked David to lead the next charge personally
They requested David to choose a new commander
They suggested David seek peace with the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: They told David not to go out to battle anymore to preserve the 'light of Israel'
questions.explanation: According to 2 Samuel 21:17, David's men swore that he should no longer go out to battle so he would not risk losing Israel’s guiding light, emphasizing the biblical principle of valuing and protecting godly leadership.

questions.question: Which giant was slain by Sibbechai the Hushathite during the battle at Gob?
questions.correctAnswer: Saph
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 21:18 states that Sibbechai the Hushathite killed Saph, one of the sons of the giant, during battle at Gob, illustrating the courage of David’s servants in facing formidable enemies.

questions.question: What unique physical characteristic is mentioned about the giant slain by Elhanan at Gob?
options: He was the brother of Goliath and had a spear like a weaver's beam
He had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot
He wielded a sword weighing three hundred shekels
He was twice as tall as any other giant
questions.correctAnswer: He was the brother of Goliath and had a spear like a weaver's beam
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 21:19 describes that Elhanan killed the brother of Goliath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam, emphasizing the formidable nature of David’s adversaries and the power of God working through His servants.

questions.question: What physical anomaly did the giant from Gath have according to 2 Samuel 21:20?
options: Six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot
questions.correctAnswer: Six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot
questions.explanation: Verse 20 reveals a giant with twenty-four digits in total, highlighting the extraordinary and intimidating nature of enemies Israel faced, and pointing to God’s power in enabling victory despite overwhelming odds.

questions.question: Who killed the six-fingered giant from Gath, and what does this demonstrate about the people of God?
options: Jonathan, son of Shimea, David’s brother, showing that God empowers His people to overcome giants
David himself, demonstrating his leadership in battle
Sibbechai the Hushathite, known for slaying giants
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan, son of Shimea, David’s brother, showing that God empowers His people to overcome giants
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 21:21 states that Jonathan killed this giant, indicating that God equips His people, not only leaders like David, to stand against formidable enemies, teaching faith and courage.

questions.question: What happened to the four giants born to Gath mentioned in 2 Samuel 21:22?
options: They were all slain by David and his servants
They ruled over Israel for a time
questions.correctAnswer: They were all slain by David and his servants
questions.explanation: Verse 22 records that these four giants fell by the hand of David and his men, symbolizing God's deliverance through faithful obedience and courage in battle.

questions.question: What does the account of Rizpah’s watch over the bodies teach us about Christian faithfulness?
options: It exemplifies steadfast devotion and honoring the dead even under hardship
It shows that mourning should be private and hidden
It teaches that vengeance is the highest priority
It instructs believers to abandon impossible causes
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies steadfast devotion and honoring the dead even under hardship
questions.explanation: Rizpah’s actions in 2 Samuel 21:10-11 demonstrate unwavering loyalty and faithfulness, encouraging believers to remain devoted and respectful even in difficult circumstances.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 21:14 demonstrate the relationship between obedience and God’s blessing on the land?
options: After obeying the king’s command to bury the bones, God was intreated for the land, ending the famine
God blessed the land before the bones were buried
The land remained cursed despite burial
The burial led to more conflict with the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: After obeying the king’s command to bury the bones, God was intreated for the land, ending the famine
questions.explanation: This passage shows that obedience to God’s commands, even in difficult matters like burial, results in divine blessing and mercy, illustrating the principle in verses 12-14.

questions.question: True or False: David spared Mephibosheth, son of Jonathan, because of the oath between David and Jonathan.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 21:7 explicitly states David spared Mephibosheth due to the LORD’s oath between David and Jonathan, highlighting the importance of faithfulness to promises.

questions.question: True or False: The seven sons of Saul who were given to the Gibeonites all survived the hanging and were later released.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 21:9 clearly states that all seven sons were hanged and died, indicating the seriousness of atonement and justice for Saul's actions.

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 21.

questions.question: Who rescued David when Ishbibenob, the giant's son, sought to kill him?
questions.correctAnswer: Abishai
questions.explanation: Abishai, son of Zeruiah, rescued David by killing Ishbibenob as recorded in 2 Samuel 21:17.

questions.question: What did the men of David swear about Abishai after he saved David?
options: He shall never go out to battle again
He would be king after David
He would lead all future battles
He would be captain of the guard
questions.correctAnswer: He shall never go out to battle again
questions.explanation: The men of David swore that Abishai would not go out to battle again so he would not quench the light of Israel (2 Samuel 21:17).

questions.question: Where did the battle occur in which Sibbechai the Hushathite killed Saph?
questions.correctAnswer: Gob
questions.explanation: The battle where Sibbechai slew Saph took place at Gob as stated in 2 Samuel 21:18.

questions.question: Who killed the brother of Goliath the Gittite?
questions.correctAnswer: Elhanan
questions.explanation: Elhanan son of Jaareoregim, a Bethlehemite, slew the brother of Goliath, as explained in 2 Samuel 21:19.

questions.question: What was unique about the man of great stature in Gath mentioned in this chapter?
options: He had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot
He was twice the height of other men
questions.correctAnswer: He had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot
questions.explanation: The giant from Gath had twenty-four digits in total, six on each hand and foot, as described in 2 Samuel 21:20.

questions.question: Who killed the man of great stature that defied Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan son of Shimea
questions.explanation: Jonathan, brother of David, killed the giant who defied Israel, as recorded in 2 Samuel 21:21.

questions.question: How many giants born in Gath were killed by David and his servants?
questions.correctAnswer: Four
questions.explanation: There were four giants born in Gath who fell by David and his servants according to 2 Samuel 21:22.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage recounts David’s battle with Goliath, related to the giants mentioned here?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Samuel 17
questions.explanation: David’s famous battle with Goliath is detailed in 1 Samuel 17, which connects to the giant theme in 2 Samuel 21:15-22.

questions.question: The term 'giant' in Hebrew used here is 'rapha'. What does this term imply in the cultural context?
options: A race of ancient warriors of great size
questions.correctAnswer: A race of ancient warriors of great size
questions.explanation: 'Rapha' refers to a class of ancient giants or mighty men, often seen as remnants of an earlier age, according to 2 Samuel 21:16-22 and Deuteronomy 2:20-21.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in 2 Samuel 21:15-22 to highlight the repeated battles against giants?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Inclusio is used here by framing multiple giant battles to emphasize the continuing conflict theme, as exemplified throughout 2 Samuel 21:15-22.

questions.question: True or False: Rizpah's mourning included guarding the bodies of the executed sons from birds and beasts until rain fell.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Rizpah spread sackcloth on a rock and prevented birds and beasts from touching the bodies until rain fell, as described in 2 Samuel 21:10.

questions.question: True or False: Mephibosheth, son of Jonathan, was put to death along with the other sons of Saul to satisfy the Gibeonites.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David spared Mephibosheth because of the oath between David and Jonathan, as stated in 2 Samuel 21:7.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of covenantal oath protecting Mephibosheth in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Samuel 20
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 20 details the covenant between David and Jonathan, explaining the protection of Mephibosheth in 2 Samuel 21:7.

questions.question: What was the reason given by the LORD for the famine during David's reign?
questions.correctAnswer: Because Saul slew the Gibeonites
questions.explanation: The famine was due to Saul's bloodguilt in killing the Gibeonites, as revealed in 2 Samuel 21:1.

questions.question: Which passage in the New Testament reflects Jesus as the true 'light of Israel', a phrase used in this chapter related to Abishai?
questions.correctAnswer: John 8:12
questions.explanation: John 8:12 identifies Jesus as the light of the world, paralleling the phrase 'light of Israel' in 2 Samuel 21:17.

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What was the reason given by the LORD for the three-year famine during David's reign?
options: Because Saul and his house had slain the Gibeonites
Because David had sinned against the LORD
Because the Israelites had broken the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Because Saul and his house had slain the Gibeonites
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 21:1 states that the famine was due to Saul and his bloody house having slain the Gibeonites, which was the direct cause of God's judgment.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 21:2, who were the Gibeonites in relation to Israel?
options: A remnant of the Amorites not of Israel but sworn to by Israel
A tribe of Israel allied with Saul
Descendants of the Canaanites who worshipped Baal
Philistines who lived among the Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: A remnant of the Amorites not of Israel but sworn to by Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 2 explains that the Gibeonites were not Israelites but a remnant of the Amorites, and Israel had sworn an oath to them.

questions.question: What did the Gibeonites refuse to accept from Saul's house as atonement according to 2 Samuel 21:4?
questions.correctAnswer: Silver or gold
questions.explanation: The Gibeonites explicitly said they would not accept silver or gold from Saul or his house as atonement, emphasizing a demand for justice rather than payment (verse 4).

questions.question: What was the specific demand of the Gibeonites for making atonement as stated in 2 Samuel 21:6?
options: Seven sons of Saul to be given to them for hanging
David to build a temple for them
Seven elders of Israel to be sacrificed
questions.correctAnswer: Seven sons of Saul to be given to them for hanging
questions.explanation: In verse 6, the Gibeonites demanded seven sons of Saul to be handed over and hanged as a form of atonement for Saul's actions.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by David sparing Mephibosheth according to 2 Samuel 21:7?
questions.correctAnswer: The faithfulness to covenantal promises
questions.explanation: David spared Mephibosheth because of the LORD's oath between David and Jonathan, illustrating the doctrine of God's faithfulness to His covenant promises (verse 7).

questions.question: What does Rizpah's actions in 2 Samuel 21:10 reveal about human response to injustice and death?
options: A profound mourning and protective love even in extreme suffering
A call for rebellion against the king
Indifference to the fate of the dead
questions.correctAnswer: A profound mourning and protective love even in extreme suffering
questions.explanation: Verse 10 describes Rizpah protecting the bodies of her sons from scavengers in sackcloth, showing deep maternal mourning and dedication despite great hardship.

questions.question: How does David's retrieval and burial of Saul and Jonathan's bones in 2 Samuel 21:12-14 reflect biblical themes about the dead and covenant?
options: Honoring the dead and fulfilling covenant obligations
questions.correctAnswer: Honoring the dead and fulfilling covenant obligations
questions.explanation: David's actions in verses 12-14 demonstrate honoring Saul and Jonathan by proper burial, fulfilling covenantal respect and bringing closure that leads to God's mercy on the land.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by the LORD's acceptance of the land's restoration after the burials in 2 Samuel 21:14?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy and justice
questions.explanation: Verse 14 concludes that after the king's commands were fulfilled and the burials performed, God was entreated for the land, showing His merciful justice.

questions.question: What theological significance can be drawn from the repeated battles against the Philistines mentioned in 2 Samuel 21:15-22?
options: The ongoing spiritual and physical struggle between God's people and their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: The ongoing spiritual and physical struggle between God's people and their enemies
questions.explanation: Verses 15-22 narrate continued conflicts with Philistines, symbolizing the persistent struggle between God's covenant people and opposing forces, a theme throughout Scripture.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 21:16-17, what doctrinal lesson is taught by Abishai saving David from Ishbibenob?
options: God's providential protection over His anointed king
The futility of trusting human warriors
The importance of physical strength over faith
questions.correctAnswer: God's providential protection over His anointed king
questions.explanation: Abishai's intervention to save David, God's anointed, highlights divine providence and protection over those He has chosen (verses 16-17).

questions.question: How does the mention of giants and their defeat by David's servants in 2 Samuel 21:18-22 contribute to the biblical narrative?
options: Emphasizes God's power working through David and his men against formidable enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Emphasizes God's power working through David and his men against formidable enemies
questions.explanation: The defeat of giants by David's servants (verses 18-22) demonstrates God's empowering of His people to overcome seemingly insurmountable foes, reinforcing His sovereignty.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do 2 Samuel 21:5-6 and 2 Samuel 21:11 convey about justice and intercession?
options: Justice requires punishment of sin, but intercession can lead to mercy and restoration
Justice is only punitive without hope of restoration
Intercession is unnecessary when justice is served
Justice and mercy are mutually exclusive
questions.correctAnswer: Justice requires punishment of sin, but intercession can lead to mercy and restoration
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 show the demand for justice by punishing Saul's sons, while verse 11 shows Rizpah's intercession through mourning, which leads David to respond, illustrating a balance of justice and mercy.

questions.question: What theological insight arises from combining 2 Samuel 21:1 and 2 Samuel 21:14 regarding sin, judgment, and restoration?
options: Sin brings judgment on the land, but repentance and proper atonement lead to God's restoration
Human actions have no effect on divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: Sin brings judgment on the land, but repentance and proper atonement lead to God's restoration
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows sin (Saul's actions) causing famine, while verse 14 shows that after proper burial and atonement, God is entreated to restore the land, demonstrating this theological principle.

questions.question: What synthesis about God's justice and covenant faithfulness can be drawn from 2 Samuel 21:7 and 2 Samuel 21:14?
options: God's justice is tempered by covenant faithfulness, preserving life where oaths exist
Covenants are made only with kings
Faithfulness to covenant excuses all sins
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice is tempered by covenant faithfulness, preserving life where oaths exist
questions.explanation: David spares Mephibosheth due to covenant faithfulness (verse 7) while still carrying out justice for Saul's house (verse 14), showing that God's justice includes honoring His covenants.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the harsh punishment of Saul's descendants in 2 Samuel 21:6-9 contradicts God's mercy. What does 2 Samuel 21 actually teach about divine justice and mercy?
options: That God's justice requires accountability for sin but is accompanied by mercy through covenant faithfulness and restoration
That God is only wrathful and merciless
That human ideas of justice apply directly to God
That mercy negates the need for justice
questions.correctAnswer: That God's justice requires accountability for sin but is accompanied by mercy through covenant faithfulness and restoration
questions.explanation: The passage shows punishment for Saul's house due to sin (verses 6-9) but also includes mercy in sparing Mephibosheth and restoring the land (verses 7 and 14), illustrating the balance of justice and mercy in God's character.
